description:
FILED s518d (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-17) from #3283 (Capture-Tiny's four badtie files).  SILENT WRONG, pre-existing (main 5c5a5679 alike).

A `local` that is NOT the first term of its statement is dropped without a word: the localization never happens and the statement's other terms run.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s518d/pr/cl3.pl):
    our $g = 1;
    sub f { print "g=$g\n" }
    { my %l; $l{o}++, local($g), $g = 2 if 1; f(); }
    f();
perl 5.40.3: `g=2` `g=1`.  PCL: `g=2` `g=2` -- the emission is `(progn (p-post++ ...) $g (p-scalar-= $g 2))`: `local($g)` lowered as a plain read of $g.  The glob spelling is the same: `$l{o}++, local(*STDOUT), open(STDOUT, ">&=1") if COND;` emits `(p-make-typeglob "main" "STDOUT")`.

WHERE IT BITES: Capture::Tiny's _capture_tee (lib/Capture/Tiny.pm:336-347) localizes the standard handles exactly so:
    $localize{stdout}++, local(*STDOUT), _open( \*STDOUT, ">&=1") if $do_stdout && tied *STDOUT && $] >= 5.008;
With the local dropped, the `_open` reaches the OUTER tie's OPEN (t/lib/TieEvil.pm dies "unimplemented"), so t/20-stdout-badtie.t, 21-stderr-badtie.t, 22-stdin-badtie.t, 24-all-badtied.t stop after row 1 (perl: 583 rows each).  s518d made the runtime half work (#3203: a bare `local *STDOUT` now gives the scope a handle with no IO; #3208: `open(STDOUT, ">&=1")` now works) -- this is the remaining blocker, and it is in the COMPILER.

FIX SHAPES (a ruling is wanted -- this is statement-lowering, near the `local ... if COND` machinery, Pl/Parser.pm ~4521-4710 / p-local-maybe / p-local-glob-if):
 (a) a statement-level comma list in VOID context whose top-level terms include a `local` lowers as a SEQUENCE: the terms before the local run, then the local opens a scope that covers the remaining terms AND the rest of the enclosing block (exactly the scope a leading `local` gets).  With a statement modifier the condition is evaluated ONCE, first, into a temporary, and each piece is guarded by it (the condition must not be re-evaluated: in Capture::Tiny it is `tied *STDOUT`, which the local itself makes false).
 (b) refuse loudly (a drop announcement / rule-12 die) for a `local` in any expression position the lowering does not handle (a non-void comma list, an argument `f(local $x = 1)`), so the silence ends even where (a) does not reach.
Acceptance: the reproducer = perl; the four Capture-Tiny badtie files run to their plan (tools/run-dist-t.pl ~/.cpan/build/Capture-Tiny-0.50-0 t/20-stdout-badtie.t); a guard row for the scalar, the glob and the conditional spelling.


=== DONE (s519a) ===
Commit 92235804 (m0).  Parser2 `_lower_local_terms` (a pre-pass over the document): (a) a VOID comma list holding a `local` term splits into one statement per term, each guarded by the modifier's condition evaluated ONCE into a fresh lexical; (b) a `local` that is the first thing its statement evaluates (an argument, a my-init, a deref block, an if/unless/while/until first condition, `+(EXPR)->` via a temp base) hoists as `local OPERAND;` before the statement; (c) every other `local` term is a ruled REFUSAL at its statement (`PCL: local in this expression position is not supported (#3370)`), announced at transpile, trappable at run time.  Signature defaults left alone -> #3410.  Found on the way and fixed: #3411 (`local *STDOUT` in a non-main package localized Foo::STDOUT).
BAR: the reproducer + glob + conditional spellings = perl (Pl/t/local-term-01.t, 9 rows, 7 fail on a074452f); Capture-Tiny badtie 20/21/22 run 559 of 583, 24 563 of 587 (were 1 row each; the 24 fails per file = #3327); perl-tests/multideref.t 53 -> 61 passing (local const/pkg/lexical/general indices 3 now restore), the only sweep mover; corpus-diff 7 of 111 (array chop local method min_local multideref split -- each a hoist or the one refusal at multideref.t:220 `@{1, local $x[0][0]}`, a row that already failed).

=== s520 (s519a resumed; Fable's rulings 3 + 4 of s519 applied) ===
The m0 refusal killed every Moo class (Role::Tiny 307 `$x = $h{$k} and ((local @{$x}{@c}), (delete @{$x}{@c}),);`).  RULING 3: `COND and/&& (LIST);` (`or`/`||`: unless) and `COND and/or local ...;` are the modifier shape and take the SAME split (Parser2 _split_void_local_list + _logical_local_list): COND evaluated once into a temporary, each term guarded, the local a leading local under a modifier, restored at the enclosing block's end.  It needed two leading-local fixes on the way: the cast spelling of an element / slice through a reference (`local @{$r}{@k}`, `local ${$r}{k}` -- it localized `@{$r}` whole and died "Can't localize through a reference") and p-local-hash-slice (a slice whose key list is an array / qw localized ONE key, the stringified vector).  Pl/t/moo-01.t 15/15 again; guard rows Pl/t/local-term-01.t 8-11.  RULING 4: the residue dies only in a VALUE position (Parser2 _local_value_consumed, sharing _stmt_in_value_position with the split); in a VOID position it reads unlocalized and ANNOUNCES `PCL: local in an unsupported expression position at F line N -- not localized`; the site scan and the residue shapes are #3414.  RULING 1: the hoist invariant is one comment at _hoist_local_term + ir-spec; guard row 12.  Pre-existing finds filed: #3415 (`local $h{a}{b} = V`, `local $r->@{...}` localize the wrong slot).
subject: A local that is not the first term of its statement is silently dropped (`$x++, local($g), $g = 2 if C` / `..., local(*STDOUT), open(...)`): no localization, the rest runs -- the Capture-Tiny badtie blocker
